'''Jamal Daniel Shead''' ({{IPAc-en|ʃ|ɛ|d}} {{respell|SHED}}; born July 24, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]].

==Early life and high school career==
Shead began his high school career at [[John B. Connally High School]] before transferring to Manor High School.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baldwin |first=Chris |title=Manor Mal — Houston’s Jamal Shead Is An Athletic Marvel Hiding In Plain Sight, But His Peyton Manning Level Leadership Leaps Out |url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/jamal-shead-houston-manor-mal-peyton-manning-leader-uh/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=Paper City Magazine |date=February 8, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 18.1 points, 6 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game as a junior. Shead led Manor High School to the state tournament for the first time in school history and scored 44 points in a win over [[Rudder High School]], earning District 18-5A Most Valuable Player honors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Welcomes Three on Signing Day |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2019/11/13/houston-mens-basketball-welcomes-three-on-national-signing-day |website=[[Houston Cougars]] |access-date=February 10, 2024 |date=November 13, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 19.3 points and 4.3 assists per game, helping Manor achieve a 28–10 record and the District 18-5A title.<ref>{{cite news |last=Jones |first=Thomas |title=History already made, Manor seeks elusive state title |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/06/history-already-made-manor-seeks-elusive-state-basketball-title/53189043007/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=March 6, 2019}}</ref> Considered a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by the [[247Sports]] Composite, Shead committed to playing college basketball for [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] and [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Quinn |first=Brendan |title=Jamal Shead was always a Houston player. Now the Coogs are his team |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4329774/2023/03/23/jamal-shead-houston-coogs-ncaa-tournament/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Shead averaged 3.3 points and 1.5 assists per game, logging minor minutes as a backup point guard on [[2020–21 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston's 2020–21 Final Four team]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Duarte |first=Joseph |title=Houston’s Jamal Shead is on point when it comes to pressure and Sweet 16 |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Houston-s-Jamal-Shead-is-on-point-when-it-comes-17024076.php |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=March 23, 2022}}</ref> In [[2021–22 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|2021–22]], Shead's sophomore season, he averaged 10 points and 5.8 assists per game. During the season he was promoted to the starting lineup after injuries to starting guards [[Marcus Sasser]] and [[Tramon Mark]]. Shead paced Houston's offense as the Cougars won both the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) [[2021–22 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|regular-season]] and [[2022 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|tournament]] championships. In the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Shead averaged 15 points per game en route to an Elite Eight berth for the Cougars, which included an upset of South Regional No. 1 seed [[2021–22 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] in the Sweet 16, in which Shead led his team with 21 points.<ref>{{cite web |last=Freeman |first=Tristan |title=NCAA Basketball: Ranking the top 25 team backcourts for 2022-23 season |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2022/07/18/ncaa-basketball-ranking-top-25-team-backcourts-2022-23-season/26/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=February 10, 2024 |date=July 18, 2022}}</ref> Shead was named to the All-AAC Third Team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2022/3/8/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men’s Basketball Honors|website=theamerican.org|language=en|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 10.5 points, 5.4 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game. Shead was named to the All-AAC Second Team and earned AAC Defensive Player of the Year honors. Following the season, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] but ultimately returned to Houston for his senior season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Harris |first=Terrance |title=UH guard Jamal Shead withdraws NBA Draft |url=https://defendernetwork.com/sports/professional/uh-guard-jamal-shead-withdraws-nba-draft/ |access-date=February 10, 2024 |work=The Houston Defender |date=June 3, 2023}}</ref> In [[2023–24 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|2023–24]], their first year in the [[Big 12 Conference men's basketball|Big 12]], Shead led the Cougars to a [[2023–24 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|regular-season]] title with averages of 12.9 points, 6.3 assists and 2.2 steals per game. He was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year, becoming the first player to win both awards in the same season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Duarte |first=Joseph |title=UH's Jamal Shead wins Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/uh-jamal-shead-basketball-naismith-defensive-19390406.php |access-date=March 11, 2025 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=April 7, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Toronto Raptors (2024–present) ===
In the [[2024 NBA draft]], Shead was selected with the 45th overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He was traded on draft night along with [[Davion Mitchell]], [[Aleksandar Vezenkov]] and a 2025 second-round pick to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Jalen McDaniels]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Chidley-Hill |first=John |date=2025-03-11 |title=Rookie guard Jamal Shead growing into leadership role on Raptors |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/article-rookie-guard-jamal-shead-growing-into-leadership-role-on-raptors/ |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312003921/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/article-rookie-guard-jamal-shead-growing-into-leadership-role-on-raptors/ |archive-date=2025-03-12 |access-date=2026-07-04 |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |language=en-CA |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}}</ref> Shead started his rookie year as Toronto's third string point guard, but was further prioritized by the mid-season trade deadline with Mitchell being sent out.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Ngabo |first=Gilbert |date=2025-04-19 |title=Inside the rise of Raptors rookie Jamal Shead: ‘It’s been impressive to watch’ |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/inside-the-rise-of-raptors-rookie-jamal-shead-it-s-been-impressive-to-watch/article_80fb1a2c-e1ea-47b3-a869-380ceeebb158.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-07-04 |work=[[Toronto Star]] |language=en-CA |issn=0319-0781}}</ref> From February 2025 onwards, his minutes and production increased as the Raptors starters dealt with injuries,<ref name=":0" /> him acting as the unit leader off the bench.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Grange |first=Michael |date=2025-04-30 |title=The kids are alright: Impressive Raptors rookies speeding up rebuild |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/the-kids-are-alright-impressive-raptors-rookies-speeding-up-rebuild/ |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season having played 74 games, averaging 7.1 points, 4.1 assists and 1.5 rebounds in approximately 20 minutes per game.<ref name=":1" /> He recorded 307 total assists, second among rookies in franchise history and fourth among rookies in the league.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> The ''[[Toronto Star]]'' wrote that despite his relatively meager statistics, his progress was "arguably the most positive development" of the season for the Raptors.<ref name=":1" />

On December 29, 2025, Shead scored 19 points in an 107-106 Raptors win over the [[2025–26 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |last3= |first3= |last4= |first4= |last5= |first5= |date=2025-12-30 |title=Jamal Shead's career-best game lifts Raptors over Magic 107-106 |url=https://www.thereminder.ca/basketball/jamal-sheads-career-best-game-lifts-raptors-over-magic-107-106-11679124 |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Flin Flon Reminder |language=en}}</ref> On January 11, 2026, Shead had a career-high team-leading 22 points in an 116-115 win over the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]]. On January 16, 2026, Shead dished out 15 points and a career-high 13 assists in an 117-121 overtime loss to the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bruce |first=Mikai |date=2026-01-17 |title=Jamal Shead records career-high 13 assists - Raptors Republic |url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2026/01/16/jamal-shead-records-career-high-13-assists/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |language=en-US}}</ref> He appeared in all 82 games (starting 12) for Toronto during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 6.6 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 5.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>
